💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that for the first time since 2014, Sacramento Republic are USL Champions.
  • In a final between two of the best teams in USL history, it had to have been the narrowest of margins that settled the outcome, with each goalkeeper making a save during the shootout before Sacramento eventually prevailed in front of its home fans.
  • RYAN SPAULDING HAS WON THE USL CHAMPIONSHIP TITLE FOR @SacRepublicFC‼️😤#USLonCBS | @bestwestern pic.twitter.com/OeFARGXyyh.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that for the first time since 2014, Sacramento Republic are USL Champions. Republic defeated Louisville City FC in a penalty shootout following a 1-1 draw Saturday at Heart Health Park, capturing the club's second title and extending its unbeaten run to 17 matches.

In a final between two of the best teams in USL history, it had to have been the narrowest of margins that settled the outcome, with each goalkeeper making a save during the shootout before Sacramento eventually prevailed in front of its home fans.

RYAN SPAULDING HAS WON THE USL CHAMPIONSHIP TITLE FOR @SacRepublicFC‼️😤#USLonCBS | @bestwestern pic.twitter.com/OeFARGXyyh.

It has been revealed that the second star comes at a symbolic moment for Sacramento Republic, which is preparing to move from Heart Health Park and into a upcoming 20,000-seat soccer-specific venue in the Railyards district of downtown Sacramento in 2028. The emotions were evident on the faces of Louisville City players after the loss as they came to terms with what happened.

According to recent reports, despite an early start to the USL Cup final in Sacramento, with kickoff at 9 a.m. local time, there was no need to wait for goals, as Louisville and Sacramento both scored within the opening 32 minutes. Cal Jennings struck in the 14th minute, while Ray Serrano answered in the 31st.

It was then the defenses that took the reins to calm the game down as Sacramento held possession to control a dangerous Louisville attack, and when Evan Davila's shootout attempt hit the post, it opened the door for Sacramento keeper Danny Vitiello to win it, and that he did.

An evenly matched final was exactly what many expected, and it delivered for Sacramento fans, who started tailgating at 5:30 a.m. and brought the energy from start to finish. Neil Collins' experienced side looked prepared for the moment, and had Mark-Anthony Kaye's effort not struck the post, Sacramento may have settled the match in regulation. Instead, it required a shootout, and that's where Republic ultimately got the job done.

A moment @SacRepublicFC will never forget 🏆✨Catch the full trophy presentation on CBS Sports! 📺➡️ https://t.co/5eh4N4wm1X pic.twitter.com/ESzeWP0IgO.

On the Louisville side, despite winning the Prinx Tires Cup during the regular season, they've now failed to win the final in three appearances since their last triumph in 2018. Considering their regular-season success, they'll want to get over the hump, but given how consistent they've been, it's impossible to say they won't be back at this stage next season.

Industry News: Why is Kai Havertz always offside for Arsenal this season?

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (909 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fourfourtwo

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Injuries hardly aided Kai Havertz last season.
  • In a recent development, in the Champions League final showdown with Paris Saint-Germain, Arteta again called on the German, and was duly rewarded as he fired the north London side in front with just six minutes on the clock.
  • Saying that, there is more to Havertz’s game than just putting the ball in the back of the net.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Injuries hardly aided Kai Havertz last season. Regardless, his standing within the Arsenal squad was evidently high. As the Gunners went in search of a first Premier League title for 22 years, he was the one who Mikel Arteta turned to during the run-in, despite Viktor Gyokeres’ substantial money summer arrival from Sporting CP.

In a recent development, in the Champions League final showdown with Paris Saint-Germain, Arteta again called on the German, and was duly rewarded as he fired the north London side in front with just six minutes on the clock. Unsurprisingly, Havertz remains the Gunners’ first-choice frontman, even if a return of three goals in the opening 10 league outings is hardly a great return.

Saying that, there is more to Havertz’s game than just putting the ball in the back of the net. The Germany international’s selflessness and impressive link-up play is a key reason behind his continued selection ahead of a more natural No. 9 in Gyokeres. Arteta wants his leading forward to drop deeper to bring teammates into play, dragging markers out of position to open up space for the wingers to exploit.

According to recent reports, and yet, his offside numbers resemble that of former AC Milan and Italy icon Filippo Inzaghi. “That lad must have been born offside,” Sir Alex Ferguson once quipped about the Italian, who addressed the comments to FourFourTwo back in 2023. In the modern day, Ferguson’s quote would be applicable to Havertz.

It has been revealed that after all, Havertz has been flagged offside 15 times in the Premier League this season. It’s almost double that of the player in second for this metric, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin (8) his closest competitor. He’s been penalised for being in the wrong place more times than four Premier League teams.

Industry observers note that for context, Bukayo Saka was caught offside more times (14) than any other player in the 2025/26 Premier League campaign. Havertz did so on just three occasions. “Certainly, it’s far too many,” Arteta said of the number of times Arsenal have been caught offside in the Premier League this season following the 1-0 win over Hull City prior to the international break.

So, for a player who is renowned for dropping deep in order to help his side in the final third, why has Kai Havertz been flagged offside so often this season?

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

According to recent reports, well, for a start, Arsenal are a team that see more of the ball than the majority of the other 19 teams in England’s top tier. Only Manchester City (65.9%) and Tottenham Hotspur (63%) have managed a greater possession share than the defending champions (59.8%) in the Premier League. A return of 1379 successful final third passes is the second-most. So, too, is 31 total through balls.

In a recent development, it’s only natural that the amount of final third passes would result in a higher number of offsides. When teams attack an opposition backline, the side on the back foot will understandably work harder to catch you offside.

Who is to blame then? Obviously Havertz is at fault but he’s making the requisite runs to try and get in on goal.

According to Opta, only Fulham’s Gonzalo Garcia (145) and Manchester United forward Bryan Mbeumo (141) have made more in-behind high-intensity runs than Havertz (125) in the Premier League this season.

Despite his gangly appearance, the former Chelsea man is deceptively quick off the mark.

Recent findings suggest that he’s playing off the shoulder of the last defender, and if those in support were prepared to release the ball a little quicker, then his runs would be capitalised upon to great effect. However, his teammates have been guilty of taking an extra touch, or taking a split-second longer to play the pass for Havertz. As such, his momentum takes him beyond the last man, meaning he either needs to check his run late, and a chance breaks down, or stray offside.

According to recent reports, of course, as things stand, Arsenal are hardly faltering domestically as a result of Havertz’s fondness for the flag. Admittedly, though, 15 goals scored doesn’t make for great reading - it’s level with Ipswich Town. And there will come a moment where these ill-timed runs and passes do have a detrimental impact on the team. “Yes, it’s something to improve,” Arteta added following the Hull triumph. It’s an concern that he concedes requires focus.

Yet Arsenal’s relentlessness combined with a watertight backline that has shipped just five goals means they are managing to get the job done.

Six of their 10 league wins have been by a single goal. A little more synchronisation between Havertz and the ammo suppliers would go a long way to give Arsenal more breathing space in their title defence.

Tech Report: Jensen Huang: Spy row, affairs leave Nvidia without its rockstar CEO

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1082 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to decide on CEO Jensen Huang's future as reports emerged of other extramarital affairs — this time with employees.
  • In a statement issued on Thursday, the world's most valuable chip supplier said Huang was resigning as President, CEO and board member, effective immediately.
  • The firm added that current Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress would become interim CEO.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to decide on CEO Jensen Huang's future as reports emerged of other extramarital affairs — this time with employees.

In a statement issued on Thursday, the world's most valuable chip supplier said Huang was resigning as President, CEO and board member, effective immediately.

The firm added that current Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress would become interim CEO.

Under Nvidia's bylaws, Huang can be removed "with or without cause" by a majority vote of its 11 directors.

The New York Times first reported that the 63-year-old Huang had an affair with a senior Nvidia executive who reported directly to him.

Later Thursday, Reuters news agency alleged an intimate relationship between Huang and a second employee, citing unidentified sources.

Sources indicate that those revelations emerged just three days after Huang admitted a relationship with a Chinese woman, whom United States intelligence agencies believe was spying for China. The woman, Alice Huang — no relation — is a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm that runs artificial intelligence (AI) data centers across Southeast Asia and is a major client of Nvidia.

The US government is investigating the startup on suspicion that it secretly sent some of its Nvidia chips to China, violating Washington's curbs on high-end semiconductors.

Those advanced Nvidia processors ‌are ​used to train and run the large AI models behind chatbots and other generative AI products.

Sources indicate that megaspeed denies the allegations and on Thursday pledged to cooperate with US investigators. Huang, the alleged spy, has been barred from entering Singapore and Taiwan — a key chipmaking island.

While Nvidia's board backed its CEO after the first scandal emerged, market watchers believe the second caused too much reputational damage to one of the world's top three companies by market value.

According to The Wall Street Journal, Huang doesn't believe in formal succession planning, so with little notice, Nvidia appointed CFO Kress as interim CEO.

Bloomberg reported Wednesday that Nvidia’s board is working with advisers to identify potential permanent successors.

According to recent reports, kress, other senior Nvidia executives and members of Huang's own family have been mooted as replacements. The family members include his daughter Madison, a senior director of product marketing, and his son Spencer, who right now works in the firm's robotics division.

Rumors also abound over a longer-term solution. On India's CNBC-TV18, Jeffrey Sonnenfeld from the Yale School of Management floated former Apple CEO Tim Cook and ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt.

US President Donald Trump also backed Cook on social media, writing: "A Legend replaces a Legend.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The scandals have certainly hit Nvidia's market value. Since the first extramarital affair emerged on Sunday, the chipmaker's market capitalization has fallen by well over $600 billion to $4.2 trillion.

Industry observers note that nvidia shares were down more than 9% in premarket trading Thursday, after dropping by 10% earlier this week. Some analysts expect the stock price to struggle in the short term.

Nvidia stock hit all-time highs just a month ago as US technology giants continued to announce billions in spending on AI infrastructure.

Demand for Nvidia's advanced chips is so high, however, that many market analysts expect little impact on near-term sales.

"While Jensen [Huang] is the heart and lungs of the Nvidia story…the company and its leading-edge GPU technology will go on and [his departure] does not change the entrenched position Nvidia has in the AI Revolution chip arms race," mentioned Dan Ives, a partner, senior managing director and tech analyst at Yorkville Ives, a US-based merchant bank.

Analysts see the biggest long-term risk in strategy and execution. After all, Huang was the leader who picked which ideas Nvidia should bet heavily on and got the whole manufacturer behind them.

His sudden exit is also seen as highly disruptive to the chip designer's strong relationships with AI hyperscalers, Taiwanese chip producer TSMC and foreign governments — especially China.

Huang was Nvidia's main lobbyist on US chip export rules and persuaded US President Donald Trump to ease some curbs on China last year.

Huang is often called a rockstar CEO for his leather jackets instead of suits.

Like Elon Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, he was also seen as a key-person risk as Nvidia’s public image, strategic direction and technical decisions became closely tied to him.

Huang steered the company for more than three decades and was also respected for his hands-on involvement in product architecture and engineering decisions.

He also insisted on a flat management structure, with around 60 executives reporting directly to him.

Huang has run the company so tightly around his own technical judgment and product decisions that investors may have little sense of how it would function without him.

At the same time, Nvidia is no longer the startup Huang founded in 1993. The company has built deep expertise in chip design and software, creating a durable moat that helps protect its huge profits, which topped $120.1 billion last year.

Some analysts argue that its central role in the AI hardware buildout makes it less dependent on Huang’s day-to-day input.

China is quickly playing catch-up with the US in the global race for AI dominance.

While Chinese AI models have lagged behind the likes of ChatGPT and Claude, recent updates from DeepSeek, Alibaba and Moonshot have closed much of the gap on benchmark tests and often beat US rivals on cost and speed.

Beijing is also investing heavily in domestic chips and data centers to reduce reliance on US hardware.

The US has curbed exports to China of Nvidia's most advanced AI chips.

However, this move has only slowed the pace of China's AI ambitions.

Reuters reported Thursday that Chinese AI firms are now trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at data centers outside China, amid fears the US could further tighten restrictions on advanced chips.

Also Thursday, Beijing accused the US of using the Nvidia spying claims as a pretext to impose a technological "blockade" on China.

The concern is likely to dominate talks next week between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC gathering in Shenzhen in southern China.

Bogle escaped a red card in the win over Tottenham after injuring Mathys Tel, with the Leeds full-back receiving the threats via social media.

His club have revealed they are looking to identify those who sent messages to the 26-year-old, whose family were threatened in one of the posts seen by Telegraph Sport after the 1-0 victory.

Leeds say they are “appalled at the disgusting, racist social-media abuse Jayden Bogle suffered” and will push for punishments to be taken.

It has been revealed that the club added in a statement: “Leeds United condemns this behaviour in the strongest possible terms. There is no place for racism in football or society.

“The club will work with the Premier League and relevant authorities to identify the individuals and push for the strongest possible action to be taken against them.

Industry observers note that “Jayden has the full and unconditional support of the club and his team-mates, and we all stand with him at this time. Nobody should ever be subjected to racist abuse.”.

Daniel Farke, the Leeds head coach, described Bogle as the “softest player” in the Premier League who would never try to hurt an opponent.

Referee John Brooks did not problem a yellow card, with VAR Tony Harrington sticking with the on-field decision.

Sources indicate that “I’m confirming the on-field decision of no red card. There’s a lack of speed going into the challenge and he’s stepping into the tackle. Confirming a reckless challenge,” Harrington was quoted on the big screen at Elland Road.

Tottenham will make a formal complaint to Pro Ref over the decision not to send off Bogle.

“I haven’t watched the scenes back so I can’t give you a clear opinion, out of the game it looked a handball but the scene with Jayden was not too far away from my bench and it looked a very unlucky coming together,” Farke said.

“Fingers crossed for Mathys that he is back soon, but it looked like there was not much speed in this action, but Jayden Bogle is one of the most fair players in the country, he would never injure or foul a player on purpose because he is such a fair character.”.

Tottenham Hotspur’s purple patch of form ended with a worrying loss. Wearing their “Spurple” kit for the first time, Roberto De Zerbi highlighted a lack of character and personality from his players and refused to blame the defeat on referee John Brooks’s decision not to dismiss Jayden Bogle for leaving one of his players injured.

Spurs’ away strip is based on a 1990s design, but this performance was more Christian Gross than Jürgen Klinsmann or David Ginola. Leeds United created the better chances and eventually broke through with 11 minutes remaining when their substitutes combined for Noah Okafor to score the winning goal.

After victories against Coventry City, Chelsea and Crystal Palace, this was a blow for De Zerbi after looking to move Spurs into the European places. Leeds had not scored in 298 minutes of football, nor had they won in five previous matches, yet the Tottenham manager could barely recognise the players who had won three matches in a row.

De Zerbi had warned his team they would face a hostile atmosphere at Elland Road, but instead of rising to the challenge, Spurs were passive until it was too late.

“We didn’t win any duels, we didn’t win any one-to-ones, there was space to play and we didn’t take the right position,” De Zerbi remarked. “We didn’t show personality, we didn’t show what we are or who we are. It is part of the journey for sure. It can be normal in football but we have to be honest, if you are not honest the future is not good. If you analyse our behaviour we can become a top team.

“We worked very hard this week. We spoke all the days about the intensity, the type of game we would have found in this stadium and the atmosphere, it was not a surprise for us. Sometimes it can happen that we didn’t play the kind of game we want.”.

De Zerbi’s honesty shines a light on the amount of work that still needs to be done at Spurs. Even after three straight wins, he has refused to get carried away despite fans looking upwards towards the European places.

Sources indicate that neither did the Italian want to blame the officials for failing to send off Bogle. Brooks has history with Spurs, sending off Xavi Simons against Liverpool last season. Here, he booked De Zerbi for his protests after Bogle’s heavy challenge that forced Mathys Tel off through injury.

According to recent reports, bogle trod on his opponent’s foot before clattering into his knee, forcing the French forward off a few minutes later. “I know that Jayden doesn’t foul out of bad intentions, he is not a nasty player and is one of the softest players in the whole league,” Leeds head coach Daniel Farke remarked. “I call him my butterfly.”.

De Zerbi admitted the injury was “bad” and that Tel would now be scanned to determine the extent of the problem. The Spurs boss was upset that Pedro Porro was later booked for a similar challenge, while Bogle went unpunished – but he mentioned the referee was not the cause of the defeat.

“I was surprised because in the same position in the second half there were two different fouls, the yellow card for Pedro Porro is not possible. I don’t know if it is a red card or not on Mathys Tel but the parameter of the referee was not good enough for this in both situations,” De Zerbi remarked.

Okafor was only on the pitch for 97 seconds before he finished off a move made by Farke’s replacements. Half-time substitute Melvin Bard sent a throw-in to Harry Wilson, who had also just come on and Okafor did the rest, bursting past Rodrigo Bentancur and planting his finish into the bottom corner. It meant the home fans were singing their “I Predict A Riot” winning anthem for just the second time this season.

For Leeds, moving into the top half will lift their own hopes of challenging for Europe, such is the congested mid-table.

“For us it has been a difficult period, we are missing key players like Anton Stach, Noah, Dominic [Calvert-Lewin] has not had the easiest spell with several injury problems and it was notable to show this unity and commitment to avoid all their individual quality to score goals and reduce them to very little,” Farke added.

Industry observers note that “Our final third, the quality was perhaps not there but second half there was no doubt just one team was pushing for that win. Another clean sheet another terrific defensive behaviour.”.

Leeds United are heartbroken to learn of the passing of supporter Colin Westby at the age of 68. Colin suffered a medical emergency ahead of our Premier League fixture with Manchester United on Sunday 18 October at Elland Road. After being transferred to hospital, he was placed into a medically induced coma and sadly following a period of unresponsiveness, the decision was made to withdraw life support. Colin was a long-standing Season Ticket Holder at the club, attending matches for over 50 years. The thoughts of everyone at Leeds United are with Colin's family and friends at this sad time. We will pay tribute to Colin in the 68th minute of our next Premier League fixture with Tottenham Hotspur, on Saturday 7 November.

According to recent reports, good morning and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Leeds United and Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road. The home side, lions at night and mice in the morning, have the unenviable record of 21 top-flight matches with a kick-off time before 3pm without a win. All that extra TV moolah comes in handy but their home ground, a bearpit under the floodlights, is neutered when its denizens are yawning instead of being fired up by social lubricant.

Daniel Farke’s team started the campaign well but are now without a win in five, drawing three matches with teams beneath them in the table – Crystal Palace, Manchester United and Sunderland – and  losing to two above them, Arsenal and Bournemouth. In fairness they played well against the champions for an hour and were deservedly in the lead until Mikel Arteta turnd to his billionaire’s bench and changed the game. At Bournemouth last week they also made a decent start, had a goal disallowed for striking Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s arm and then James Trafford chucked one in.

They never recovered, found themselves increasingly bogged down when trying to unlock a low block and were mugged on the break in added time to lose 2-0. They are a robust side overly reliant on their wing-backs to create chances for their No 9 in the absence of the injured Noah Okafor who was unavailable to train with the team this week because of a groin injury but may be fit enough for the bench.

According to recent reports, spurs, by contrast, are buoyant following three wins on the bounce – over Coventry, Chelsea and Palace, two with clean sheets – that has taken them from 19th to ninth, three places above Leeds. They have won their last three visits to Elland Road, 0-4 under Antonio Conte, which proved to be the last match of Marcelo Bielsa’s glorious spell at the Peacocks, 1-4 under Ryan Mason, which sealed Leeds’ relegation, and 1-2 under Tomas Frank last year by virtue of goals from Mathys Tel and Mohammed Kudus as the home side struggled against their width back in the days before their switch to a back three.

UK court convicts 2 Iranian men of spying on journalists

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (713 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Two Iranian men were found guilty of spying on dissident journalists in Britain on behalf of Iran's Revolutionary Guard on Thursday.
  • British counterterrorism police said the case reflected intensifying hostile Iranian activity in the country, an concern that recently made headlines amid the security scare at the RAF Fairford airbase that's a major operational site in Europe for the US Air Force.
  • The men, both in their 40s, were arrested last year, with Iran repeatedly rejecting the allegations against them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two Iranian men were found guilty of spying on dissident journalists in Britain on behalf of Iran's Revolutionary Guard on Thursday.

British counterterrorism police said the case reflected intensifying hostile Iranian activity in the country, an concern that recently made headlines amid the security scare at the RAF Fairford airbase that's a major operational site in Europe for the US Air Force.

The men, both in their 40s, were arrested last year, with Iran repeatedly rejecting the allegations against them.

The Woolwich Crown Court in London convicted one of the Iranian citizens not just of spying on journalists working for the Persian-language dissident TV channel Iran International, but of plotting a violent attack against one or more of them.

The second individual had also faced charges of plotting an attack but was only convicted of spying on the reporters.

One of the convicted defendants mentioned he was acting under duress after his family was threatened, and the other said he did not know that his actions were assisting Iranian intelligence.

A third defendant, a 57-year-old Iranian man, was acquitted of all charges.

The men were accused of engaging in conduct likely to assist the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), Iran's multi-discipline military force that's seen as closer to the country's religious leadership and more influential than its regular armed forces.

The UK formally designated the IRGC as a threat to national security in July, meaning that supporting or assisting the organization can carry penalties of up to 14 years in prison as part of new rules on national security and state threats.

Sentencing in this case is still pending and is scheduled for mid-December.

"This was a calculated operation to spy on those critical of the Iranian regime," mentioned Frank Ferguson, chief prosecutor for the Crown Prosecution Service's special crime and counter-terrorism division.

The two men were accused of visiting addresses linked to their targets, taking photos and videos, and using platforms such as ChatGPT to research them online.

"Thankfully, the defendants were stopped before any attack could take place," prosecutor Ferguson noted.

Senior ‌National Coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing Vicki Evans said that the IRGC or "middlemen" for Iranian intelligence were directing the plot.

Iran's government had repeatedly denied the allegations, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying he was "disturbed" by the trio's arrests last May.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

There have been four cases targeting the Persian language television channel Iran International since late 2023.

In July, two Romanian men were jailed for stabbing a journalist outside his home in 2024.

A spokesman for the broadcaster's parent company, Volant Media, said in a statement that Thursday's verdicts "don't make the lives of our journalists any safer so long as the Islamic Republic of Iran continues its campaign of death threats and violence against them.".

Iran International reported that a British barrister was also one of the targets.

British law enforcement has been warning of an uptick of hostile Iranian activity in recent years, particularly since the US military operations against Tehran began earlier this year.

Most notably, the UK has accused Iran of being behind a suspected plot targeting the RAF Fairford base in September, after which US President Donald Trump withdrew some long-range bombers from the site.

Three men were indicted in the US in relation to that plot this week, while two others currently face charges in the UK.

According to recent reports, but beyond this, the head of Britain's MI5 domestic intelligence agency Ken MacCullum stated in October that Iran-linked operations had led to more than 50 arrests in the last year. He also said known cases of so-called state threats had more than quadrupled in a decade.

Counter-terrorism police chief Evans stated she expected this trend to continue.

France this week also accused Iran of being behind a cyberattack targeting refrigeration units at hundreds of supermarkets in October, although Iran denied any involvement.

European governments are on heightened alert for so-called hybrid warfare tactics, from Russia as well as Iran, amid the geopolitical tensions of recent years. New technologies like low-cost drones and AI are also threatening to make such activities cheaper, harder to trace, and potentially more effective.

Giving Marjorie Taylor Greene a platform isn't good for America

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 4 min read (885 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Editor’s Note:  Dean Obeidallah, a former attorney, is the host of SiriusXM radio’s daily program “The Dean Obeidallah Show.” Follow him @DeanObeidallah@masto.ai.
  • According to recent reports, last year, GOP Rep.
  • Last week, Greene’s Twitter account was temporarily suspended by the Elon Musk-headed platform over a tweet with a graphic referring to a “Trans Day of Vengeance,” as she denounced a planned transgender rights rally.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Editor’s Note:  Dean Obeidallah, a former attorney, is the host of SiriusXM radio’s daily program “The Dean Obeidallah Show.” Follow him @DeanObeidallah@masto.ai. The opinions expressed in this commentary are his own. View more opinion on CNN.

According to recent reports, last year, GOP Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene of Georgia spoke at a white nationalist event organized by Holocaust denier Nick Fuentes that caused Republican leaders to denounce her.

Last week, Greene’s Twitter account was temporarily suspended by the Elon Musk-headed platform over a tweet with a graphic referring to a “Trans Day of Vengeance,” as she denounced a planned transgender rights rally.

And come Tuesday, Greene has announced aims to protest in Fresh York City when former President Donald Trump is expected to be arraigned on an indictment of more than 30 counts, calling the proceedings against him an “unconstitutional WITCH HUNT!”.

It has been revealed that but on Sunday, Greene was featured on CBS’ “60 Minutes” in an interview the long-running show promoted on Twitter with the tease: “Republican Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene, nicknamed MTG, isn’t afraid to share her opinions, no matter how intense and in-your-face they are. She sits down with Lesley Stahl this Sunday on 60 Minutes.” The images attached to this tweet by “60 Minutes” include Greene and Stahl walking through the US Capitol, taking a stroll outside and Greene showing Stahl something on her phone.

It's time for Marjorie Taylor Greene to go.

Recent findings suggest that in the segment that aired Sunday night, Stahl noted the congresswoman had moved from the fringe to the GOP’s front row in two years despite a “sharp tongue” and “some pretty radical views” as well as “over the top” comments such as “the Democrats are a party of pedophiles.” Stahl also referred to video of Greene chasing a Parkland, Florida, school shooting survivor, still maintaining that the 2020 election was stolen and failing to criticize Trump over spending. (The interview was conducted before news of his indictment.).

But Stahl didn’t mention Greene spoke at a white nationalist event a year ago while a member of Congress or her extreme anti-Muslim views and her defense of January 6 rioters.

In a recent development, criticism of CBS for amplifying Greene has been swift and well-deserved even before the program aired. Former GOP Rep. Adam Kinzinger of Illinois tweeted beforehand: “Wow. Insane that 60 min would do this.” (Kinzinger is a CNN senior political commentator.).

Journalist Molly Jong-Fast also slammed “60 Minutes” with the tweet: “Attention is currency and 60 minutes is spending its currency on the Jewish space lasers woman.” (Jong-Fast was apparently referring to Greene’s past claim that a massive California wildfire was started by “a laser” beamed from space controlled by a prominent Jewish banking family.).

David Hogg, who survived the 2018 horrific school shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland and has since become an activist against gun violence, responded, “I look forward to your questions about why she thinks school shootings are fake and why she’s supported QAnon.”.

Trump's risky call for protests.

Greene amplified the conspiracy theory — two years before being elected to Congress — that the Parkland shooting that took 17 lives was staged. And in 2019, Greene appeared on video confronting Hogg outside the Capitol when he was championing laws to save lives from gun violence, screaming that the then-teenager was a “coward.” She also called Hogg “#littleHitler” on social media.

Greene’s own tweet promoting Sunday’s segment was not filled with her typical smears of “fake news” when she doesn’t like the coverage. Rather, Greene urged people to tune in as she praised “60 Minutes” host Stahl (and misspelled her first name): “It was an honor to spend a few days with the legendary icon Leslie Stahl and talented crew @60Minutes.” Greene added, “Leslie is a trailblazer for women in journalism. And while we may disagree on some concerns, I respect her greatly.”.

It has been revealed that now, it is true that “60 Minutes” over its 50-plus-year history has featured what the show has dubbed “controversial” guests. These include a 2000 interview with Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh, whose 1995 terrorist attack left 168 dead, including 19 children. And the show did a 1979 interview with Iran’s Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini.

Perhaps “60 Minutes” views Greene — who has repeatedly downplayed and even defended the January 6, 2021, attack plus called for the GOP to become the party of “Christian nationalism” — in the vein of its long list of controversial guests. (CBS had not responded to a request from CNN for comment at time of publishing.).

Join us on Twitter and Facebook.

However, the choice of Greene as a guest instantly recalls the comments of then-CBS CEO Les Moonves during Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign when he admitted that Trump’s candidacy “may not be good for America, but it’s damn good for CBS.” Moonves added, “The money’s rolling in and this is fun. … (T)his is going to be a very good year for us,” concluding, “Sorry. It’s a terrible thing to say. But bring it on, Donald. Keep going.”.

Moonves may be gone from CBS, but it appears his mindset continues at “60 Minutes.” And that may be good for “60 Minutes,” but it’s definitely not good for America.

#82985. Chelsea must toughen up against Leeds – or risk being ‘bullied’ again

Chelsea must toughen up against Leeds – or risk being ‘bullied’ again

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (957 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later?
  • Chelsea have a No 9 problem at both ends of the pitch.
  • According to recent reports, defeat at Sunderland brought accusations that Chelsea’s defence was susceptible to being “bullied”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Chelsea have a No 9 problem at both ends of the pitch. Up top, Xabi Alonso is struggling to find a solution in the absence of Joao Pedro, who has still not returned to training after weeks out with a thigh problem. And at the back, Alonso’s porous defence appears fallible in the face of the old-school striker’s revival.

According to recent reports, defeat at Sunderland brought accusations that Chelsea’s defence was susceptible to being “bullied”. The primary bully, in this case, was frontman Brian Brobbey, one of the Premier League’s most imposing units. His overpowering of Levi Colwill led to Sunderland’s controversial penalty that proved the difference two weeks ago.

According to recent reports, alonso didn’t agree with such a critique at the time. "Not bullied, I would say that it was a situation that we could have defended better,” he stated after the match at the Stadium of Light. But amid Chelsea’s frantic form, questions are being asked whether Alonso’s back line can handle the Premier League at its most physical.

Sources indicate that in this regard, Saturday’s test of Leeds provides the ultimate test. There are few teams in the top-flight as physical as Leeds, even if Daniel Farke may sometimes opt to play down his players as “butterflies”, like he did for Jayden Bogle after the right-back avoided a red card for a challenge on Tottenham’s Mathys Tel.

It has been revealed that leeds have won the most duels in the Premier League this season; Farke’s players are not scared of going in for a challenge. That has made them a particularly difficult team to score against, conceding a mere eight goals so far. Chelsea have let in double that tally, with only Arsenal and Brighton conceding fewer than the Whites.

Alonso isn’t only learning of English football’s physical requirement now; his five seasons at Liverpool would have taught him as such. And he knows that if his team continue to be beaten in this department, it will repeatedly cost them in this league regardless of the opposition. “It’s the Premier League. It’s not newly introduced,” Alonso said. “It’s not just against Leeds. It will happen next week against Forest, and the next one against Palace. This is the level of the competition.”.

In a recent development, ever the tactician, Alonso does not put full emphasis on brute physicality – even if it is a necessary step to unlocking quality. He continued: “It’s not just the duels – it’s about a football thing or tactical thing. When you have good control, normally you are in better positions to press and duel. When you don’t have that much control, you aren’t in that good position. It’s not just ‘one v one, let’s see what happens’. No, you can help situations to be stronger in duels. After, it’s the individual qualities that help.”.

In a recent development, leeds nevertheless appeared to lean into the criticism in the build-up to their trip down south. They posted a compilation of their best moments against the Blues from over the years, which included its fair share of crunching tackles and Chelsea mistakes. Whether a statement of intent or merely mind games, Alonso noted his side was only focusing on themselves. “We focus on not being soft tomorrow and being competitive,” he said. “That’s our goal.”.

Recent findings suggest that like Sunderland, Leeds’ main threat comes in the form of a traditional No 9. Dominic Calvert-Lewin may have been studying tape of Chelsea’s last outing and licking his lips this week, knowing that he has the capacity to cause the same sort of problems as Brobbey.

Sources indicate that “We prepare knowing that we have prepared because it’s a player with different qualities but the same kind of profile,” Alonso noted. “It’s nothing fresh. It’s quite common in the Premier League that they have a good No 9.

Recent findings suggest that “Calvert-Lewin is doing well. He played with England. But it is up to us, how we defend, how we compete in those situations, how we attack the last line, how we attack their defenders. The preparation has, as always, we think been good. We are ready for tomorrow.”.

Sources indicate that back in fashion, the target man profile is giving Chelsea’s young defence trouble. While Alonso’s arrival at Chelsea coincided with the move away from their chaos of youth, his back line remains fresh-faced. His five first-team centre-backs have an average age of 23, with Maxence Lacroix the oldest at 26. They all came into senior football with the old-school No 9 being just that, and the leap back in time has forced them to adapt.

In a recent development, so far, the learning curve has been apparent. But Alonso doesn’t believe his players lack the tools to deal with what used to be the norm up top.

Asked if centre-backs have forgotten how to defend the traditional No 9, Alonso replied: “No, I don’t think forgotten. But it’s demanding to play against No 9s. They have good movement in the box, out the box. But this is the demand. You can ask the full-backs, they have to play against great wingers in one v one situations. But I don’t think it’s been forgotten.”.

Alonso is personally happy to see the revival of the No 9. “It’s good they are back, these type of players,” he noted. Whether he still feels the same after the visit of Calvert-Lewin and the rest of Leeds’ hardmen may depend on his players toughening up to the task.

#82983. 'It looked like every star in the sky was falling': Eyewitnesses remember the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1517 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Space ↗ Open Full Page

'It looked like every star in the sky was falling': Eyewitnesses remember the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1517 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 17-18, 1966, the Leonid meteor storm thrilled stargazers during one extraordinary night when the stars themselves looked as though they were falling from the sky.
  • Recent findings suggest that at the peak of the shower, observers at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona estimated an astonishing 40 meteors per second streaking across the sky.
  • According to recent reports, it's hard to imagine what it was like to experience such a spectacle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Overnight Nov. 17-18, 1966, the Leonid meteor storm thrilled stargazers during one extraordinary night when the stars themselves looked as though they were falling from the sky.

Recent findings suggest that at the peak of the shower, observers at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona estimated an astonishing 40 meteors per second streaking across the sky. That's 2,400 shooting stars per minute, or a staggering 144,000 per hour. It was a spectacle that many regard as the greatest meteor display in recorded history.

According to recent reports, it's hard to imagine what it was like to experience such a spectacle. But who better to tell us than those who saw it with their own eyes? To mark the 60th anniversary of the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966, we asked those who saw it to share their memories.

"I was around 9 years old at the time of the 1966 Leonid storm, living a few miles east of Roxie, Mississippi. We lived in a rural, dark, relatively remote area with almost zero outside lights.

According to recent reports, "I and a couple cousins were spending the night at our Uncle and Aunt's house, staying up late, just fooling around outside like young kids do when living in the 'sticks'. As we walked down a road, I remember hearing an almost constant series of little whistling, zipping sounds. The sounds were similar to when you light a nylon rope on fire and as it burns, little flaming droplets drip down with a zippy sound.

"I looked up and the sky was filled with streaks of 'shooting stars' and I realized that was what made the sounds. I yelled at my cousins to look up and we could hardly believe what we saw. We all laid down on our backs and for a couple of hours just watched and listened to what seemed like 1000's of 'shooting stars' zipping and zinging overhead. I could even smell the sulphur-like odor from the burning little bits of space dust.

"I'm nearly 70 years old now but I'll never forget that experience. I always knew what I'd seen that night was special but not until much later in life, after the internet, did I realize just how lucky I was to have experienced that storm. That night was one of the most loved and memorable nights of my life and I'll treasure it forever.".

"I was an astronomy lab assistant at Southwestern College in Winfield, KS, in 1966, majoring in physics and math and the physics professor was sure that the Leonids would be an amazing shower worth the class time.

According to recent reports, "The sky was clear. He called me early the morning of the 17th and told me to get to the campus. I can't remember the exact time as students and faculty were pounding on doors to get people, including neighbors,to watch.

"We were all lying in an open grassy area because that was the best way to see the whole sky. It was like a humongous fireworks display and lasted even as the sun began to rise.

"As years have gone by, I have felt grateful and privileged to have seen such a wonderful astronomical event.".

"I was 18 and spent the night in El Paso, Texas, lying on the ground in my backyard and watching. It looked like every star in the sky was falling. It was amazing!".

Industry observers note that "I was 9 years old and was camping with my dad in the western mountains of California. We were set up to sleep outside, but on this particular night, we saw more meteors than I have ever seen before or since. We watched them all night and didn't get much sleep.".

It has been revealed that "Brooklyn Center, Minnesota. 14 years old. Watched in our front yard. The sky was full. It took your breath away".

"I was 3 years old at the time of the 1966 Leonid meteor shower. I remember very little at that age, but watching the sky fall that night was seared in my memory.

"My family was living in Troy, Alabama, at the time. My father, a professor of psychology, was a man of science with a special love of astronomy, which he passed onto his young son.

Industry observers note that "He drove us several miles out of town until the skies were dark, without interference from the lights of the town. Troy was much smaller then and it was easy to find dark, clear skies.

According to recent reports, "I remember that it was a little chilly that night. My father and I stretched out on the hood of the car, the warmth of the engine radiating against our backs.

According to recent reports, "That night was my first meteor shower, and only many years later did I learn that year's Leonids were historic. Sadly, though I bore witness to the display, we missed the true event by several hours as I grew tired by 1:00 AM, and my father had to teach class in the morning.

According to recent reports, "I remember many bright, colorful, and long-trailed meteors. Some left 'tails' that hung in the sky for several seconds. We only experienced the beginning of the event, but it is a core memory with my father.

"That night/morning spoiled me for future meteor watches; I assumed they would all be as interesting.".

It has been revealed that not everyone was lucky enough to witness the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966. For some, the night was memorable for an entirely different reason.

Space.com columnist Joe Rao was just 10 years old at the time, and despite eagerly anticipating the display, the weather had other ideas.

Industry observers note that "Standing in my backyard late on a Wednesday night in the Throggs Neck section of The Bronx, cursing the heavens. My grandfather stood at my side, just shaking his head and murmuring two words over and over: 'Too bad.'.

"Clouds covered the midnight sky like a fresh coat of plaster, smearing my view of the Leonids. My mom, sister and grandmother, as well as my neighbors had long since trudged to bed, leaving only Grandpa and I to gaze at a charcoal gray sky totally devoid of stars.".

It has been revealed that rao had been looking forward to the storm ever since a visit to Latest York's Hayden Planetarium, where astronomer Fred C. Hess had encouraged visitors to look out for what could be a spectacular display.

But when Rao and his grandfather ventured outside, there wasn't a single star in sight.

"After a few minutes, I sobbed to my grandfather, 'But they promised it was only going to be partly cloudy tonight.' To which he sadly replied, 'I guess the party is over.'".

The Leonid meteor shower occurs every November when Earth passes through a stream of debris left behind by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years.

As tiny particles of comet dust enter Earth's atmosphere at speeds of around 44 miles (71 kilometers) per second, they burn up and produce brilliant streaks of light we know as meteors, or shooting stars.

In a recent development, most years, the Leonids produce relatively modest displays with around 10 to 15 meteors per hour under ideal viewing conditions. But occasionally, Earth encounters a particularly dense trail of debris, triggering a meteor storm.

Recent findings suggest that the Leonids have a long history of putting on some spectacular displays, with significant storms recorded in 1833 and 1866. And 1966 wasn't the last time the Leonids put on an extraordinary show. In 1999, 2001 and 2002, the Leonids once again reached meteor-storm levels, producing thousands of meteors per hour at their peaks. The indicates aren't over yet! With comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle due to return in 2031, astronomers are already looking ahead to what the following years could bring.

In a recent development, A study released in August 2026 predicts potentially impressive Leonid displays in 2033 and 2034, with peak rates exceeding 1,000 meteors per hour. However, these forecasts remain uncertain, and a repeat of the extraordinary 1966 storm is far from guaranteed.

For now, we'll just have to wait and see.

Daisy Dobrijevic joined Space.com in February 2022, having previously worked as a staff writer for All About Space magazine. She completed an editorial internship with BBC Sky at Night Magazine and worked at the National Space Centre, communicating space science to the public.

It has been revealed that daisy holds a PhD in plant physiology and a Master's in Environmental Science. Based in Nottingham, U.K., she covers all things space, with a special focus on solar activity and space weather. She also has a keen interest in astrotourism and is always on the lookout for the next northern lights adventure.

She will join Hurtigruten as an onboard astronomer for a northern lights sailing in January 2027.

#82980. John Toshack on Bill Shankly, Liverpool and an extraordinary football career

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 15m • 📚 Deep Dive (2911 w)

John Toshack on Bill Shankly, Liverpool and an extraordinary football career

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2911 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fourfourtwo

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, bill Shankly knew how to make an instant impact on players.
  • The Welshman has never forgotten Shankly’s first words to him.
  • Over the next eight years, Toshack’s religious experience would develop him from a highly promising forward into an Anfield legend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, bill Shankly knew how to make an instant impact on players. The year was 1970 and John Toshack had just joined Liverpool from Cardiff for a club-record £110,000 fee, when he was greeted by his newly introduced manager.

The Welshman has never forgotten Shankly’s first words to him. “I was only 21 and didn’t have a driving licence, so I travelled from Cardiff by train,” Toshack recounts to FourFourTwo. “Bill Shankly was waiting for me at the station, with his trilby on his head. The first thing he noted to me was, ‘Welcome to Liverpool, son: you’ve come out of school to come to church’.”.

Over the next eight years, Toshack’s religious experience would develop him from a highly promising forward into an Anfield legend. That day at Liverpool Lime Street station, his extraordinary life in football was just getting started.

Recent findings suggest that today, 55 years later, following a career that took him to a dozen countries, he lives in Besalu – a village of medieval architecture in Catalonia, not far from the French border – with his wife, Mai, and several dogs they’ve adopted. As a manager, Toshack had seven spells in Spain: three at Real Sociedad, two with Real Madrid, plus stints at Deportivo La Coruna and Real Murcia. He welcomes FFT into his rural home, telling us he used to read the magazine when he lived in the UK.

Time hasn’t eroded a single detail of his extensive career, right back to his school days in his home city of Cardiff. “I’d take my sandwich with me so I didn’t have to go home for lunch – it meant I could stay and play football in the playground,” explains Toshack with a smile. Not just football, either: “I played cricket during the week, rugby on Saturday mornings and football in the afternoon,” he adds.

According to recent reports, then the first scouts appeared. At 15, he received an offer from Tottenham to go to London for trials. “I went with two other team-mates to a residence next to the old White Hart Lane,” he recalls. “We trained, and I thought they were going to give me a chance. But when I returned home, I got a letter thanking me but saying they didn’t believe I was good enough. I was gutted.”.

His father, George, was a carpenter; a self-made man from Scotland. Young John’s mother encouraged him not to drop out of school, wanting him to have an alternative if he didn’t achieve his ultimate goal of becoming a footballer. Toshack, however, soon began breaking barriers locally. His first-team debut for Cardiff came aged 16, against Leyton Orient. Back then, only one substitution was allowed per team. “I came on with 10 minutes to go and scored a goal,” he indicates. “I can still visualise it today, if I close my eyes. A week later, we travelled up north to Middlesbrough. I started and scored two goals in 20 minutes. We won 4-3. It was a dream start.”.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Making a name for himself in the Second Division, Toshack caught the eye of Fulham in 1968. “Bobby Robson came in with an offer of £60,000, which was good money at the time,” he says. “But I thought London was too big for a boy from South Wales, and turned it down. The Cardiff management were outraged at my decision. The transfer would have been a big money-spinner for them.”.

Toshack would score exactly 100 goals for Cardiff, in 207 appearances. More approaches were inevitable. In 1970, one arrived from Liverpool, who were attempting to return to the summit of English football after title triumphs under Shankly in 1964 and 1966. Cardiff boss Jimmy Scoular lived down the road from Toshack, and delivered the news. “I saw him one Sunday morning and I knew he wanted to tell me something key,” continues Toshack. “He had read the papers, and they noted Liverpool were coming for me. Shankly had offered £110,000, which was a record amount. Jimmy told me that we couldn’t say no. I thought, ‘This time, I’m ready’. Besides, Liverpool wasn’t Fulham.”.

In a recent development, anfield awaited. “There was a lot of expectation,” admits Toshack. “In those days, we barely warmed up – we’d come out five minutes before kick-off and you could hear You’ll Never Walk Alone. The noise was deafening.”.

His debut was rushed: he had suffered a minor ankle injury in his last game for Cardiff, but media expectation and his own desire to pull on a Liverpool shirt won out. “The following week, after treatment, it was the Merseyside derby against Everton,” he indicates. “It couldn’t have been better. There were 54,000 supporters in the stands, 27,000 of them behind the Kop, all on their feet. I scored my first goal with a header from Steve Heighway’s cross, against Everton’s centre-back, Brian Labone. That’s when my love story with Liverpool began.”.

Playing at Anfield never ceased to be a thrill. “We liked to attack the goal at the Kop end in the second half, in front of all of those fans, but other clubs knew that and tried to win the toss to spite us,” says Toshack, chuckling. Not long after the 6ft 1in striker’s arrival, a fellow young forward called Kevin Keegan signed from Scunthorpe United. A famous partnership was born.

Recent findings suggest that “Shankly put us together in attack in training, and there was great chemistry between the two of us from the start,” notes Toshack. “Keegan would say to me, ‘Anywhere you like, Tosh’. I’d jump up with a smile on my face, as I knew that if I won the jump and touched the ball, he’d find it for a finish.

Sources indicate that “We understood each other so well that we were once invited onto a TV show to see if telepathy existed between us. They put our backs to each other and we had to guess the colour or the number of a paddle that the other one held up. I saw them reflected in the camera. I got them all right and he got none. He was scared! I said to him, ‘You see which of us is the clever one: you run but I’m the one who gets it right here!’”.

The duo would combine for six years, thanks to Shankly’s decision to pair them up. “I owe almost everything to Shankly and to Liverpool,” indicates Toshack. “He was basic, direct and uncomplicated in his message. He was sharp, provocative and liked to pick on Everton. He’d say, ‘Everton play so bad that if they played in my garden, I would draw the curtains so I couldn’t see them’.”.

In 1973, Shankly’s Liverpool won the league and the UEFA Cup, the club’s first European silverware. After the final, the manager asked his players to come to his office to renew their contracts, one by one. “I noted to him, ‘Boss, I’ve been top scorer; I’m on £80,000 and I think £90,000 would be good’,” Toshack tells FFT. “He said, ‘Ninety? No. You deserve £100,000’. I left his office excited, but before I got to the car, I thought, ‘He’s cheated me – he was going to give me more’. Years later, I spoke to him and he admitted it: he was going to give me £120,000! That was Shankly.”.

Sources indicate that shankly’s assistant, Bob Paisley, took over when he retired a year later. “They were the perfect blend,” states Toshack. “But I always got the feeling that Paisley wasn’t a big fan of mine. He tried to sell me to Leicester in 1974, but as well as being a coach, he was a physiotherapist, and he could see that I was beginning to get muscle calcification. That’s what thwarted my departure.”.

Still with years on his contract, but weakened by physical challenges, Toshack modified his game, becoming more selective about when to expend energy. “I knew that Keegan was much better alongside me – without me, he wouldn’t score so many goals – so I learned to think more,” he says. “Those were my first steps as a coach.”.

Sources indicate that two more league crowns followed at Anfield, although Toshack missed out on Liverpool’s victorious 1977 European Cup Final due to injury. Less than a year later, having plundered 96 goals for the club, he negotiated his release to move into coaching at the age of 28. That coaching career could have begun back at his old club, Cardiff, had manager Jimmy Andrews not rejected his initial enquiries, saying he wasn’t sufficiently qualified to join the club’s backroom staff. Instead, Toshack spoke to Cardiff’s rivals, Swansea, and was soon appointed player-manager of the Fourth Division club. He became the Football League’s youngest manager.

It has been revealed that what ensued was quite remarkable: ascension to the third tier within two months, then another promotion a year later, courtesy of a goal from their boss on the last day of the season. “I was a substitute: number 12 on the bench,” he remembers. “The ground was full – 22,000 spectators – and we had to beat Chesterfield to go up. We went 1-0 down, then we were drawing, and I knew I couldn’t feature for more than 30 minutes. I had my assistant on the bench giving me the elbow, saying, ‘Hey, something has to be done...’ With 15 minutes to go, without warming up or anything, I mentioned, ‘Come on, I’m going on’. Three minutes later: a cross from the left wing, I jumped and... goal!”.

Incredibly, Toshack led Swansea into the top flight two seasons later. Sealing promotion away at Preston meant that in the three years and 62 days after his appointment, Toshack – still only 32 years of age – had taken the Swans from the Fourth Division to the First Division.

“We had to win – no other result would do,” he tells us. “I invited Shankly, who had played more than 300 matches for Preston. He gave a talk to my players in the hotel and they listened attentively; he was almost a god-like figure. Some 15,000 Swansea fans came all the way from Wales, and we did it. Nobby Stiles, Preston’s manager, very graciously came over to congratulate me.”.

Sources indicate that the rise continued. Swansea – in their first ever top-flight season, barely seven years on from needing re-election to the Football League – led the First Division as late as the final week of March, before eventually finishing sixth. In an early 2-2 draw at Anfield, an already-significant fixture for the ex-Liverpool man became particularly poignant when Shankly died in the week of the match. “The day before the game, I carried his coffin with three other team-mates,” indicates Toshack. “I was in shock – totally speechless. I wore a Swansea tracksuit during the game, but with a Liverpool shirt underneath.”.

His dream, of course, was to manage the Reds one day. “I was close – very close,” he states. “I went to Liverpool and Paisley told me that he had to stay for another year because of his pension. I’d already spoken to secretary Peter Robinson and chairman John Smith in a private room in a hotel in Southport.

“I’d told the Swansea chairman it was my last season. I thought it was done. But Liverpool went for Joe Fagan and I had to go back to Swansea. From then on, nothing worked out and Swansea were relegated. I lost my motivation.”.

It has been revealed that toshack needed a reset. After a year at Sporting in Portugal, he found happiness in Spain (“It’s been many years,” he notes now, but I feel so loved and recognised here”). He won the Copa del Rey in the first of three spells with Real Sociedad, then switched to Real Madrid in 1989. “It was a difficult start, as we lost to Barcelona at the Camp Nou, then were knocked out of the European Cup by Milan,” he reflects. “We lost 2-0 at San Siro, then won 1-0 at the Bernabeu. It was one of the greatest games of my coaching career. We couldn’t go crazy – we had to get back into the tie little by little – but to beat that team, with Frank Rijkaard, Marco van Basten and Ruud Gullit, was almost impossible.”.

Real Madrid won La Liga in Toshack’s first season, scoring a then-record 107 goals. “There were some critics who remarked we were too defensive…” he laughs. Things didn’t go as well in his second spell, 10 years later. Arriving in February 1999, he took Los Blancos from sixth to a second-placed finish, but they were eighth early in the subsequent campaign when Toshack publicly slated goalkeeper Albano Bizzarri after a defeat to Rayo Vallecano. Asked by president Lorenzo Sanz to retract his comments, Toshack refused, chirping, “There’s more chance of a pig flying over the Bernabeu.” He was soon sacked.

Recent findings suggest that “That sentence will stay with me for life – just like the one about the usual 11 bastards, which was Shankly’s,” he indicates. “Shankly stated, ‘John, don’t think about picking the team for the next game on a Saturday night after losing, because you’re going to leave everyone out. On Sunday, ‘these two... they’re not bad’. When Wednesday comes, you prepare the team with the same 11 bastards as last week’.”.

It has been revealed that toshack’s face lights up when recalling his experience managing Wales from 2004 to 2010. He’d briefly led his nation in 1994, combining the job with his role at Real Sociedad, but resigned after 47 days. When he returned a decade later, replacing Mark Hughes, wins weren’t forthcoming but he believes he laid the foundations for future generations. “From day one,” indicates Toshack, “I made it very clear to the FAW that we may not qualify for the World Cup in Germany or the Euros in Austria and Switzerland, but with the under-21 coach, Brian Flynn, we were starting to give opportunities to youngsters like Aaron Ramsey, Joe Allen, Sam Vokes and, of course, Gareth Bale. Gareth was the chosen one.”.

Sources indicate that by then, Toshack had also managed in France with Saint-Etienne and in Italy with Catania. He headed to even more unexpected locations in the final years of his coaching career. He spent a year as manager of Macedonia (now North Macedonia), only for the relationship to break down because he didn’t want to live in the country; then came Khazar Lankaran in Azerbaijan. “It’s nice to feel the respect they have for you in more remote places,” he says. “My time there was short-lived, but I’m very fond of it.”.

Sources indicate that he also cherishes his two years in the Moroccan city of Casablanca, at the helm of Wydad. “We filled the stadium with 70,000 fans an hour before a match against Raja,” he claims of the derby with Wydad’s city adversaries. “There are few places where I’ve experienced hotter atmospheres. We won the league title in 2015 but the following season, in the semi-final of the African Champions League, I was sacked.” Facing Zamalek in the first leg in Egypt, Wydad trailed 2-0 at the interval. “At half-time, I knew I was out – the doctor told me,” he says. “Our first and second goalkeepers were doing military service and the Moroccan government didn’t give them permission to play.” Wydad lost 4-0.

In 2018, Toshack signed a three-year deal with Tractor in Iran, but lasted only three months. “Someone reported me and my assistant for wearing shorts out in the street,” he lamented. “We were summoned to a police station. When we got there, all of the policemen were waving at us and asking for photos. As we climbed up the stairs, though, the atmosphere became more tense, until we reached the top, to the office of the captain. He greeted us loudly and rudely because wearing shorts is associated with homosexuality.”.

The players were easier to manage. “We didn’t have to give out a single fine,” he says. “If the training session was at 10am, the kids were sitting and waiting at 9.30. They were very orderly.”.

According to recent reports, toshack hasn’t returned to football since. In February 2022, he spent nine days on life support inside a Barcelona hospital, suffering from a severe case of pneumonia caused by COVID. “I don’t remember much of that,” the 75-year-old tells FFT now. For his wife, however, it was terrifying experience. “John was dead,” explains Mai. “We were going on holiday to Majorca, but before we left home he just collapsed. We called for an ambulance and he was rushed off to hospital. They told us he was short of oxygen and that he’d also punctured a lung.

Sources indicate that “Emilio Butragueno, a great friend of the family, called us every day.” Butragueno, once Toshack’s star striker at Real Madrid, sent a physical trainer to assist the Welshman in his recovery. “It was slow, but here we are,” indicates Mai.

“Here we are – the same bastards as always,” adds her husband. Bill Shankly taught him well.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cancers arising in distinct organs differ in their cellular organization, genetic alterations and patterns of how they progress1. Now, a large-scale analysis reveals striking similarities between the non-malignant cells found in the tumour microenvironment (TME) — the local environment in and around a tumour, in which non-malignant cells interact with cancer cells — across various types of cancer. Writing in Nature, Januszyk et al.2 integrate single-cell data from 42 types of tumour in humans and mice. The authors identify recurring patterns of gene activity in immune cells and in stromal cells, which contribute to tissue structure and function. These similarities provide a starting point for testing whether treatments directed at the non-cancerous cells of the TME might be effective across a range of cancer types.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Harry Kane faces the "next few months" on the sidelines after suffering a torn left ankle ligament during Bayern Munich’s 1-1 draw against Cologne on Friday.

The injury occurred when Cologne defender Joel Schmied intercepted Michael Olise’s low cross at the back post, clattering into the Ballon d’Or winner’s left leg on the follow-through.

Though the England captain got back to his feet after treatment, he was unable to continue and hobbled off the pitch accompanied by two physios.

Following an assessment by the club’s medical team, Bayern confirmed Kane had sustained a torn syndesmotic ligament and "will therefore be sidelined for the next few months".

It is a major setback for Kane, who won the Ballon d’Or last month and then became the most-capped England men’s player of all time last week, surpassing the previous record held by Peter Shilton.

Kane scored 73 goals last season to earn the Ballon d’Or and had made a flying start to the current campaign, registering 10 goals and 10 assists in 16 games for Bayern across all competitions.

He also scored eight goals in six Nations League games to help England top their group as he took his overall international tally to 93 goals in 127 caps.

England learned on Friday that they will face Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals, which will be a rematch of the two teams meeting at the same stage of the World Cup back in July.

Thomas Tuchel’s side won that game 2-1 thanks to a brace from Jude Bellingham, and the two-legged quarter-final will be played in late March.

Kane will hope that he is back in time for that tie, but Bayern’s statement indicates that he will not be seen on the pitch for the remainder of 2026 or the early weeks of 2027.

Bayern also suffered another injury blow on Friday night as Michael Olise failed to return for the second half. The club issued an update on Olise’s condition after the game.

The statement read: “Michael Olise has been diagnosed with a contusion of the foot. The French attacking player will receive treatment over the coming days.”.

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:52 EST, 21 November 2026.

Luca Williams-Barnett will score better goals. That was the consensus on a day when the Tottenham starlet marked his first Premier League by scoring the first and creating the second.

Roberto De Zerbi compared him to Lamine Yamal after watching the 18-year-old steal the show as Spurs beat Ipswich, their fourth win in five to move within three points of the top four.

It has been revealed that 'He is a special player, I am not surprised,' said De Zerbi. 'I decided 10 days ago he would play and I asked him two things. First, to play like he is on the park with his friends and then to work hard without the ball, like Raphinha and Yamal.

'In football today players with talent have to work hard and attackers are the first defenders.'.

Asked if Williams-Barnett could aspire to the levels of Barcelona’s Yamal, the Spurs boss replied: 'Yes, I think so'. And told how on the teenager had spent the bus ride to the stadium watching clips of Ronaldinho, Neymar and Eden Hazard on YouTube.

His goal was a picture of youthful desire and determination to get across his marker at the back post and be first to a delicious teasing cross delivered by Pedro Porro.

Roberto De Zerbi rates Williams-Barnett as ‘one of the best’ young players he has worked with.

Williams-Barnett slid and stretched past Abdoul Ouattara with his right foot as the ball skipped and hit him high on the left thigh before rebounding into the bottom corner.

Sources indicate that you make your own luck. The Spurs crowd erupted. They have been waiting to hail another of their own. Maybe this is the one. A goal on his first start, just like Harry Kane, and at 18 years and 51 days, the club’s youngest league scorer since Gareth Bale.

Industry observers note that there has been a buzz growing around Williams-Barnett for the last 18 months as he rose through the academy ranks. He made his England Under-19 debut in September, coming on as a sub for Max Dowman, Arsenal’s teenage sensation.

De Zerbi adores his attitude as much as his talent, and a confidence bordering arrogance on display in pre-season when he dinked in a ‘Panenka’ style penalty in a shootout in Australia.

He is right-footed but started against Ipswich wide on the left, in the role no player has made their own since Heung-min Son.

Dominic Solanke, who scored Tottenham's second goal, congratulates his young team-mate.

Williams-Barnett might have had a second before half time, a half-chance miscued and a header saved.

Spurs fans responded. When he picked up the ball on halfway early in the second half, they roared him forward into the space ahead. He duly obliged, through the gears into a swagger and into the Ipswich penalty box without meeting a challenge.

Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Kinsky 6; Porro 7, Van Hecke 6, Senesi 6, Udogie 6 (Robertson 80); Fernandes 7, Gallagher 7; Kudus 6, Maddison 7 (Bergvall 64, 5), Williams-Barnett 8 (Savio 64, 6 (Gray 90)); Solanke 7 (Marmoush 64, 5).

Scorers: Williams-Barnett, Solanke.

Booked: Maddison, Williams-Barnett, Kudus, Fernandes.

Ipswich (3-4-2-1): Walton 7; Furlong 5, Diop 5, O’Shea 6; Outtara 4 (Fatawu 56, 5), Palacios 5 (Florentino 56, 5), Lukic 6, Davis 6 (Greaves 82); Enciso 5, Maeda 5 (Clarke 56, 5); Flemming 6.

Recent findings suggest that belatedly, Darnell Furlong tried to hold him up. But Williams-Barnett made a yard on the outside and whipped over a cross with his left foot, which fizzed past Walton and was turned in from close range by Dominic Solanke.

The teenager booted the ball jubilantly into the crowd and collected his first yellow card from killjoy referee Rob Jones.

Sources indicate that williams-Barnett left to a standing ovation when he was replaced by Savio in the 64th minute. 'Luca was magnificent,' said Solanke. 'To see him do that on his first Premier League start is crazy.'.

It has been revealed that spurs coasted in. It had been comfortable, even without some senior players including Sandro Tonali who had been unwell.

According to recent reports, they were solid at the back and creative up front, peppering the Ipswich goal with 18 shots. Mohamed Kudus struck a post from a first-half free kick, won by Williams-Barnett.

Christian Walton made strong saves to deny James Maddison and prevent Dara O’Shea turning into his own goal.

Savio cross hit a post with a deflected cross before he was struck down by a recurrence of the hamstring injury which ruled him out for six weeks. It was the only blemish for De Zerbi, although one to enhance the opportunities ahead for Williams-Barnett.
